headline: Trump bans three news outlets from the White House
summary: He announced it Friday on Truth Social, saying CNN, MS NOW and Politico "constantly write or report fiction or lies," and gave no examples. He did not say how the ban would work. Reporters from CNN and Politico were still on the grounds afterward. Asked why now, he said, "You get sick of it," and allowed a court might not let it stand.
cover_answer: It ends up in court. CNN sued last time and got back in.
table_question: Should you get to pick who is allowed to ask you questions?

5-7.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
5-7.script: The president said three news companies can't come into the White House anymore. He says they tell lies about him, but he didn't show any. It's like telling three kids they can't come in your room because you're mad at them. The grown-ups have it.
5-7.why: Shutting someone out because you don't like what they say is a thing a five-year-old already knows from home.
5-7.why_long: Shutting someone out because you do not like what they said is a five-year-old’s own move, which is why the script uses it. No explaining of the press. Expect “is he allowed?” Maybe not, and the script says a court might stop it, which is the useful part: somebody else gets to check.

8-12.script: Trump posted that CNN, MS NOW and Politico are banned from the White House for writing "fiction or lies." He gave no examples and no rules for how it works. Like a referee ejecting players without saying what the foul was.
8-12.why: Kids this age want the rule named before the punishment. Here there isn't one.
8-12.why_long: This age wants the rule named before the punishment, and here there is no rule and no example. That gap is the story, and the script points at it rather than filling it in. Expect “what did they write?” He did not say. Sitting with that is the lesson, and it is an uncomfortable one.

13-17.script: Is that even legal? Trump says a court may not let the ban stand and did it anyway: "good to point it out, whether it survives or doesn't." He named no false story. What's the point of a ban you expect to lose?
13-17.why: Teens can hold a move and its stated reason side by side and judge the gap.
13-17.why_long: He said a court might not let it stand and did it anyway. A teenager can hold the move and its stated reason side by side and measure the gap, which is the skill this story is for. The script quotes him rather than characterising him. Ask what the point of a ban you expect to lose might be.

5-7.a: He says they tell lies about him. He didn't give any examples. Reporters ask presidents hard questions, and that's their job.

8-12.a: He says so. When he barred a CNN reporter in his first term, CNN sued and got the pass back.
He didn't say. His post named no story. Asked why now, he said it was cumulative stories over the last few years.

13-17.a: It ends up in court. CNN sued over a first-term ban and won the pass back. The AP's 2025 suit is still going.
He says they "constantly write or report fiction or lies." No example. Others may follow.
